_strings.@@11e62ff332c1: Treaty conformity — GA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from GA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the GA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Georgia conforms. The resident return (Form 500) starts from federal adjusted gross income (2024 Form 500, Line 8: "Federal adjusted gross income (From Federal Form 1040)" with the warning "Do not use FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME"), and adjustments are made only on Form 500 Schedule 1. The 2024 Schedule 1 ADDITIONS (lines 1-5) are limited to: (1) Interest on Non-Georgia Municipal and State Bonds, (2) Lump Sum Distributions, (3) Depreciation, (4) Net operating loss carryover deducted on the Federal return, and (5) Other (Specify) — there is NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA add-back). To the contrary, the 2024 IT-511 booklet expressly lists as a SUBTRACTION item: "Income from any fund, program or system which is specifically exempted by Federal law or treaty." Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and GA neither adds it back nor otherwise re-taxes it (and explicitly recognizes the treaty exemption), it flows through untaxed.

_strings.@@29c443fcee9e: Qualified Caregiving Expense Credit (Credit Code 204) — Taxpayers who pay qualified caregiving expenses for a qualifying family member who is at least age 62 OR has been determined disabled by the Social Security Administration. A qualifying family member includes the taxpayer or someone related to the taxpayer by blood, marriage, or adoption. Qualified services (home health agency, personal care, personal care attendant, homemaker, adult day care, respite care, medically necessary equipment/supplies) must be obtained from an organization or individual NOT related to the taxpayer or family member. Expenses already subtracted/excluded from Georgia net taxable income do not qualify.
_strings.@@2be0e3aab5c6: Child and Dependent Care Expense Credit (Credit Code 202) — Georgia taxpayers who claimed and were allowed the federal child & dependent care expense credit under Internal Revenue Code Section 21 on their federal Form 1040. The Georgia credit is a flat percentage of that allowed federal credit; the booklet does not impose a separate Georgia income limit (federal Section 21 eligibility rules govern).
_strings.@@44a3d7314703: Disabled Person Home Purchase or Retrofit Credit (Credit Code 201) — A permanently disabled person (the taxpayer or the taxpayer's spouse on a joint return) who has been issued a permanent parking permit (or special permanent parking permit) by the Department of Revenue, and who purchases a new single-family home containing all four required accessibility features, or retrofits an existing single-family home with one or more of those features (no-step entrance; 32-inch interior passage doorways; bathroom-wall reinforcements for grab bars; accessible light switches/outlets).

There is no separate nonresident return number; the residency status box on Form 500 Line 4 (1=full-year resident, 2=part-year resident, 3=nonresident) designates status.

_strings.@@8a9091a33112: Low Income Tax Credit — Georgia residents whose Federal adjusted gross income (FAGI) is less than $20,000 and who are not claimed (or eligible to be claimed) as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal or Georgia return. Cannot be claimed by an inmate in a correctional facility. Part-year residents qualify only if they were Georgia residents at the end of the tax year. Credit is computed per exemption (self, spouse, and natural/legally adopted children, plus one extra per taxpayer/spouse 65 or older; for this credit dependents do NOT include unborn dependents with a detectable heartbeat). Must be claimed on or before the end of the 12th month following the close of the tax year.

_strings.@@d0106885bb14: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW CREDIT for 2024 — the Georgia Resident Itemizer Tax Credit: full-year residents (and part-year residents living in Georgia at the end of the year) who itemized deductions may claim up to $300 per taxpayer on Form 500 Line 19. The credit cannot exceed the Line 16 tax liability and cannot be carried forward. It did not exist for 2023. Resolve via: 2024 IT-511 booklet, What's New and the Form 500 Line 19 instructions at the citation URL (this pack's `credits` block carries the transcribed $300 cap and eligibility).

citation.source: Georgia DOR, 2024 IT-511 Individual Income Tax Instruction Booklet — What's New: 'Effective January 1, 2024, the income tax rate is 5.39%. Additionally, personal exemptions have been repealed except for the $4,000 dependent exemption. Finally, Georgia standard deductions have increased to $24,000 for Married filing jointly returns and $12,000 for Single, Head of household, and Married filing separately returns'; Line 11 standard deduction chart (Married filing jointly $24,000; Single, Married filing separately, Head of household, Qualifying surviving spouse $12,000 each); Line 14 'Multiply the number of dependents on Line 7c by $4,000'; Line 16 'Multiply the amount on Line 15c by 5.39%. Round to nearest dollar.' Second pass: the 2024 Form 500 itself prints Line 11 'Enter $12,000 if the filing status from Line 5 is A, C, or D. If the filing status is B, enter $24,000', Line 14 'Enter the number from Line 7c. Multiply by $4,000', and Line 16 'Tax (Multiply Line 15c by 5.39%. Round to the nearest dollar)' (https://dor.georgia.gov/document/document/2024-500-individual-income-tax-return-blank-form-printing/download) — both passes agree.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 500, Line 16: 'Tax (Multiply Line 15c by 5.39%. Round to the nearest dollar)'. Line 15c Georgia Taxable Income = Line 10 Georgia AGI minus Line 11 standard deduction (or Line 12c itemized), minus Line 14 dependent exemption (Line 7c x $4,000), minus Line 15b Georgia NOL utilized. This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 STRUCTURAL CHANGE — GEORGIA WENT FLAT: 5.39% of Georgia taxable income for ALL filing statuses (What's New: 'Effective January 1, 2024, the income tax rate is 5.39%'), replacing the 2023 1%-5.75% graduated schedules. Personal exemptions are REPEALED (the 2023 $2,700/$3,700 per-status amounts are gone) except the dependent exemption, now $4,000 (2023: $3,000). Standard deductions are now $24,000 MFJ and $12,000 for everyone else (2023: $5,400/$7,100/$3,550 + exemptions). The 2023 pack's folding trick (shipping standard deduction + personal exemption as a combined $8,100/$14,500/$7,250 figure) NO LONGER APPLIES — the shipped standard_deduction is the printed Form 500 Line 11 amount, verbatim. Base guidance: Supply Form 500, Line 10 'Georgia adjusted gross income' (Line 8 federal AGI from Form 1040, net of Line 9 adjustments from Form 500 Schedule 1) for a FULL-YEAR resident. The op subtracts the per-status Line 11 standard deduction and $4,000 per dependent (Line 14) to reach Line 15c Georgia taxable income (assuming no Line 15b NOL), then multiplies by 5.39%. Pass exemptions_count=0 — Georgia has NO personal exemption for 2024 (repealed); pass dependents_count = Form 500 Line 7c (qualified dependents plus unborn dependents). Do not use this op if you itemize deductions, claim a Georgia NOL (Line 15b), or file as a part-year resident/nonresident (they omit Lines 9-14 and use Schedule 3, which prorates the deduction) — compute those on the form. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE: Georgia files QSS under filing status D 'Head of Household or Qualifying Surviving Spouse' with a $12,000 standard deduction (both the 2024 Form 500 Line 5 status list and the IT-511 Line 11 chart, which prints 'Qualifying surviving spouse $12,000') — pass head_of_household to this op, NOT married_filing_jointly. The engine's default QSS->married_filing_jointly mapping would apply MFJ's $24,000 and UNDERSTATE tax. AGE-65/BLIND ADDITIONAL DEDUCTION GONE: the 2023 $1,300-per-checkbox additional standard deduction (old Form 500 Line 11b) is NOT printed anywhere on the 2024 Form 500 or in the 2024 IT-511 Line 11 instructions — the flat $12,000/$24,000 amounts are the entire standard deduction. No age_65/blind keys ship for 2024. ITEMIZERS NOT MODELED: if you itemized on your federal return (or are MFS and your spouse itemizes), you MUST itemize on the Georgia return (Line 12c = federal Schedule A total less Georgia adjustments) and the standard deduction does not apply. NEW for 2024: itemizing residents may claim the Georgia Resident Itemizer Tax Credit of up to $300 per taxpayer on Form 500 Line 19 — a CREDIT against Line 16 tax, not a base reduction, and not modeled. NO tax table and NO rate schedule for 2024: Line 16 is a straight multiplication printed on the form ('Multiply Line 15c by 5.39%. Round to the nearest dollar') — the 2023 booklet's per-status Tax Rate Schedules and $100-band Georgia Income Tax Table no longer exist. Georgia NOL not modeled: Form 500 Line 15b (Georgia NOL utilized, limited to 80% of Line 15a income for losses from tax years 2018+) is subtracted before Line 15c taxable income. Part-year residents and nonresidents not modeled: they omit Form 500 Lines 9-14 and use Schedule 3, which prorates the standard deduction and dependent exemption by the Georgia-income ratio. This pack's subtractions apply only to full-year residents. Taxpayers required to file federal Form 1040NR generally may NOT take the Georgia standard deduction (2024 IT-511: most are allowed only the limited Form 1040NR itemized deductions). CREDITS (subtracted from tax, NOT modeled and NOT base reductions): Low Income Credit (Form 500 Line 17 — a per-exemption CREDIT of $5-$26 for federal AGI under $20,000); Other State(s) Tax Credit (Line 18); Georgia Resident Itemizer Tax Credit (Line 19, NEW for 2024, up to $300 per itemizing taxpayer); IND-CR series 200 credits (Line 20); Schedule 2 series 100 credits (Line 21). Total credits used (Line 22) cannot exceed Line 16 tax. Rounding: the Form 500 Line 16 instruction itself mandates 'Round to the nearest dollar'; this pack rounds half-up to whole dollars (irs_round), matching the form's presentation.
